### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/scenarios`, touching **1** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`, `packages/qa/scenarios/package.json`, `packages/qa/scenarios/src/score/index.ts`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/plugins/index.mdx`  _(via tsconfig.build.json (literal, a string literal on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/index.mdx`  _(via tsconfig.build.json (literal, a string literal on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/plugin-spec.mdx`  _(via tsconfig.build.json (literal, a string literal on a changed line))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`, `packages/qa/scenarios/package.json`, `packages/qa/scenarios/src/score/index.ts`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **0** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6ddf827236902c0ccaee56b65431a4c8a9c7ac09` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5de6f21f1de3d31ee9f7c0fa0d5bdacb9ba2173f` — the merge of head `702570a3381412eb2eaacccabb37d50fb1b50dae` into base `6ddf827236902c0ccaee56b65431a4c8a9c7ac09`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5de6f21f1de3d31ee9f7c0fa0d5bdacb9ba2173f && git checkout 5de6f21f1de3d31ee9f7c0fa0d5bdacb9ba2173f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6ddf827236902c0ccaee56b65431a4c8a9c7ac09 702570a3381412eb2eaacccabb37d50fb1b50dae && git checkout -B drift-repro 6ddf827236902c0ccaee56b65431a4c8a9c7ac09 && git merge --no-ff 702570a3381412eb2eaacccabb37d50fb1b50dae

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6ddf827236902c0ccaee56b65431a4c8a9c7ac09
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6ddf827236902c0ccaee56b65431a4c8a9c7ac09` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT · #30915 · 2026-11-06T12:50Z

Head-sha: `e748dfb0a07e44016c54018d9f9591f9337428f2`

- **Shape:** 10 files (+335/−15) in `packages/qa/scenarios/**`, two README lines and one `turbo.json` line. Private package, `skip-changeset`, `Fixes #30915`.
- **Measured by the seat in the diff:**
  - A tsup build writes ESM, CJS and `.d.ts` to `dist/`, with one entry per export subpath and `splitting: false`, so each entry's externals are exactly its own graph. Every `exports` subpath now points at `dist/`. The package stays `private`. `tsup` comes from the root devDependencies, as in every other package.
  - `./score` is the narrow entry `src/score/narrow.ts`: re-exports only, with no module moved, so #30883's score edits do not collide. `./score/full` is the old `src/score/index.ts`, with the capability-tag checks and `scoreCardArtifact`, `gradeCardOperation` and `gradeCardAnswer`. Inside the repo, nothing outside the package imports `@objectstack/scenarios`. The named consumer, cloud#3604, needs only `scoreGraphShape` and the run graders, and both are in `./score`.
  - `@objectstack/scenarios#test` now depends on its own `build`, which still runs `^build` through the build task. The suites and `run-scenarios` keep reading `src/`.
  - Acceptance is pinned by `test/build/built-consumer.test.ts` (a tsup-built consumer `import()`s `./score` under plain Node) and `narrow-score-graph.test.ts` (`./score` reaches neither `objectql` nor `plugin-sharing`). The dev ablated both and saw them go red.
- **Gates:** the dev reports 256 package tests and typecheck green, and 65 derived gates of 65 at exit 0. `check-governed-merges --pr 30938`: NOT governed, 350 lines. CI is still running at this head, so auto-merge lands it on green.

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT (delta) · #30915 · 2026-11-06T13:31Z

Head-sha: `fb3e0224222b4f284998301a4aa4ef5c00b6e643`

- **Delta from `e4cfda26`:** the same test file only. The child-process recorder used to write its whole resolve record (about 139 KB) to stdout from an `exit` handler. That write does not finish draining a 64 KB pipe before the process exits, so a slow reader under CI load got a truncated JSON (job 127915847898, position 146175). The recorder now `writeFileSync`s the record to a temp file named by `SCENARIOS_RESOLVE_RECORD`, and the parent reads that file. stdout carries only the one-line verdict.
- **Measured by the dev:** the mechanism is confirmed with a slow reader (the record is lost), and the fix holds over 5 runs of test/build (5/5 each). Typecheck exits 0 and the test-file gates exit 0. No buffer or timeout was raised. Auto-merge stays armed.
